cards.text: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has dreams that trouble his spirit, and sleep escapes him. Friend, I know that night: you flip the pillow to the cold side like THAT'S gonna fix your whole life. So he summons his magicians, enchanters, sorcerers and astrologers to explain his dreams.

cards.question: The king tells his wise men his spirit is anxious to understand his dream. What do the astrologers ask him to do?

cards.text: Here's the problem. Nebuchadnezzar isn't telling them a thing, and his word is final.

cards.question: So what does Nebuchadnezzar demand from his wise men?

answers.text: Both the dream and its interpretation
Only the interpretation of his dream
A potion to help him sleep at night

cards.text: If they can't, they'll be cut into pieces and their houses reduced to rubble. That's not a performance review, friend, that's a DEMOLITION CREW.

cards.question: But if the wise men tell him the dream and its interpretation, the king promises them gifts, rewards and great ___.

cards.text: So the wise men try a second time: let the king tell the dream, and they'll give the interpretation. Ah, the classic move. When the answer's no, ask again and hope it turned into a yes.

cards.question: When the wise men ask again, what does the king say they're doing?
True or false: Nebuchadnezzar says he'll tell the wise men his dream once they prove their loyalty.

cards.text: The astrologers say no one on earth can do what the king asks. No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked anything like this of a magician, enchanter or astrologer.

cards.question: True or false: The astrologers say no one could tell the king his dream except the gods.

cards.text: That answer makes the king so angry and furious that he orders ALL the wise men of Babylon destroyed. Friend, I got slid into a junk drawer for blurry stamps, and I thought the Millers were tough.

cards.question: The decree goes out to execute the wise men. Which young men from Judah, serving in the king's palace, do the king's men come looking for too?

cards.text: When Arioch, commander of the king's guard, goes out to execute the wise men, Daniel responds with discretion and tact. Me, I'd be behind the oven yelling, 'I'M JUST A STAMPER!'

cards.question: With the execution order out, what does Daniel ask Arioch?

answers.text: Why the king's decree is so harsh
Who gave the king the idea
When the order will be carried out

cards.text: Arioch explains the situation to Daniel. Then Daniel walks right in to see the very king whose decree has men out looking to execute him.

cards.question: Standing before the king, Daniel asks him for some ___, so he can give him the interpretation.

cards.text: Daniel goes home and explains the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. I bet that was the shortest, scariest group chat in Babylon: 'Guys. Small update.'

cards.question: Daniel urges Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah to plead for ___ from the God of heaven concerning this mystery.

cards.text: During the night, the mystery is revealed to Daniel in a vision. Every wise man in Babylon said no one on earth could do it, and God hands it over before sunrise.

cards.question: Daniel now knows the king's dream. What does he do?

answers.text: He blesses the God of heaven
He runs to wake up Arioch
He writes it down on a scroll

cards.text: Daniel declares, 'Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.' Not 'look what I figured out.' Wisdom and power belong to HIM.

cards.question: In Daniel's praise, God changes the times and seasons, and He removes kings and ___ them.
True or false: Daniel says God can't see what lies in darkness.

cards.text: Daniel thanks the God of his fathers, who has made known to them the dream of the king. Then he goes straight to Arioch, the man the king appointed to destroy the wise men.

cards.question: What does Daniel tell Arioch about the wise men of Babylon?

answers.text: Do not execute any of them
Wait one more night for them

cards.text: Arioch hastily brings Daniel to the king and says, 'I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.' 'I have found a man.' Arioch, buddy, the man found YOU.
The king asks Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, if he can tell him what he saw in the dream and its interpretation. Big question, big room, BIG king.

cards.question: Before he tells the dream, what does Daniel say about the wise men, enchanters, mediums and magicians?

answers.text: None of them can explain this mystery
They knew the dream all along
They should be put in charge of it

cards.question: Daniel tells the king there is a God in ___ who reveals mysteries.
True or false: Daniel says the mystery was revealed to him because he has more wisdom than any man alive.

cards.text: Then Daniel tells the dream: 'As you, O king, were watching, a great statue appeared.' Dazzling, awesome, and I promise you, friend, it was not a lawn flamingo.

cards.question: In the king's dream, the statue's head was pure ___, and its chest and arms were ___.

cards.text: Then belly and thighs of bronze, and legs of iron. Every level a little less fancy, like me after all those years on the Millers' counter.

cards.question: At the bottom of the statue, what are its feet made of?

cards.text: As the king watches, a stone is cut out, but not by human hands. Nobody's holding a chisel on this one, friend.

cards.question: True or false: In the dream, the stone strikes the statue on its feet of iron and clay.

cards.text: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver and gold are all shattered and become like chaff on the threshing floor in summer. The wind carries them away, and not a trace of them can be found.

cards.question: The statue is gone. What does the stone that struck it become?

answers.text: A great mountain that fills the whole earth
A new statue made of solid gold
A high wall around all of Babylon

cards.text: Daniel says, 'This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.' First up, the king himself: the God of heaven has given him sovereignty, power, strength and glory.

cards.question: Daniel says God made Nebuchadnezzar ruler over people, beasts and birds. Which part of the statue is the king?

cards.text: After him comes another kingdom, inferior to his. Next, a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule the whole earth.

cards.question: Then comes a fourth kingdom, as strong as iron. What will it do to all the others?
True or false: Daniel says the kingdom pictured by the feet of iron and clay will be united and whole.

cards.text: Partly strong and partly brittle. The peoples will mix with one another but won't hold together, any more than iron mixes with clay.
Then Daniel gets to the big one. In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end.

cards.question: The kingdom the God of heaven sets up won't be left to another people. It will stand ___.

cards.text: Daniel wraps up: the great God has told the king what will happen in the future. 'The dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.'

cards.question: After hearing the dream and its meaning, how does King Nebuchadnezzar react?

cards.text: He pays homage to Daniel and orders an offering and incense presented to him. Daniel walks in on the king's execution list and ends up with the king face down in front of him. Friend, that's a COMEBACK.

cards.question: What does Nebuchadnezzar say about Daniel's God?

answers.text: He is truly the God of gods and Lord of kings
He is one god among the many in Babylon
He is the god of the exiles and no one else

cards.text: Then the king promotes Daniel and gives him many generous gifts. Execution list to the top of the org chart, and me? I once went from the counter to the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar makes Daniel ruler over the entire province of ___.
True or false: The king also makes Daniel chief administrator over all the wise men of Babylon.

cards.text: So now Daniel's the boss of the very wise men he kept from being executed. And he has a request for the king.

cards.question: At Daniel's request, who does the king appoint to manage the province of Babylon?

cards.text: The king appoints Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, the new names given to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah (Daniel 1:7), while Daniel stays in the king's court. The friends Daniel called on when things got scary get to stand with him when things get good.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling of verse 7, then 'Ah, the classic move.', then 'When the answer's no, ask again and hope it turned into a yes.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card 3 already says 'Nebuchadnezzar isn't telling them a thing.' That gives away this true/false answer, which asks whether he'll tell them the dream. The card also misses what verse 9 actually adds: the king accuses them of false and fraudulent words, and says that telling him the dream will prove they can give the interpretation.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke 'I thought the Millers were tough' makes the Millers the target and casts them as harsh. His backstory says Mother Miller never complained. The line also doesn't land clearly.

rule.text: Godly character. He never holds a grudge, and his humor reflects kindness and forgiveness.

findings.problem: This question introduces Daniel and his friends as 'young men from Judah, serving in the king's palace.' That fact comes from Daniel 1, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'The shortest, scariest group chat in Babylon' puts a modern group chat inside the Bible setting instead of keeping it as a separate comparison.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'Every wise man in Babylon said no one on earth could do it' stretches the text. In verse 10, the astrologers are the ones who say this, not every wise man.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote from verse 20, then 'Not 'look what I figured out.'', then 'Wisdom and power belong to HIM.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote from verse 25, then the repeated 'I have found a man.', then 'Arioch, buddy, the man found YOU.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card cites verse 45 but leaves out its key point: the stone cut out without human hands, which shattered the statue, is the kingdom God sets up. No card in the interpretation connects the stone to that kingdom, so the baker misses a central detail of the dream's meaning.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling of verse 46, the 'execution list' line, then 'Friend, that's a COMEBACK.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'He is truly the God of gods and Lord of kings', uses the Bible's own phrasing. The two wrong answers are plain modern wording, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling of verse 48, then 'Execution list to the top of the org chart, and me?', then 'I once went from the counter to the back of a junk drawer!'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card cites only Daniel 2:49, but it tells that Daniel is now over the wise men, which comes from verse 48. The citation should be Daniel 2:48-49.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Story cards 1, 3, 6, 7 and 9 are plain retelling with no humor at all. Several of them could carry a real laugh without muddying a fact, such as Nebuchadnezzar hearing he's the head of gold, or the iron and clay that won't mix.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
